bull.b: Multi-year NBMs with contractual guarantees improve revenue visibility and deepen strategic relationships with datacenter and Edge customers. Their rising share of bits should make the business less dependent on spot NAND pricing, while floor pricing and RPO support planning and investment.

The sharp improvement in operating and free cash flow shows that 2026 earnings are converting into liquidity rather than remaining primarily accounting profits. Sustained cash generation would support technology investment, capacity expansion, buybacks, and resilience through future industry cycles.

A rapidly expanding datacenter mix and newer BiCS and high-bandwidth products position SanDisk toward faster-growing, higher-value storage applications. This portfolio shift can improve product relevance, support stronger mix, and reduce reliance on slower consumer-oriented demand.

bear.b: The large swing from losses to exceptional profitability demonstrates that SanDisk remains highly exposed to NAND pricing, demand, and industry-cycle changes. Even with strong current results, earnings and cash flow could contract materially if pricing or utilization normalizes.

Persistent allocation indicates SanDisk may be unable to fully serve incremental customer demand over the coming periods. Supply limits can cap revenue growth, delay customer expansion, and reduce the company’s ability to convert strong market demand into additional shipments.

Greater dependence on a few strategic customers raises the impact of any change in their demand, product plans, or purchasing commitments. Long-term contracts provide visibility and guarantees, but concentration can still reduce negotiating flexibility and amplify execution risk.
